reviews.title: Commercials ads
reviews.text: It is so easy to turn away from your Bible on this app because the commercial ads interrupt your Bible study and and time with God. Also if you’re in a video call business, medical or other call the Bible alarm can knock you off the call because it automatically interrupts your screen time.

reviews.title: Temu has taken over this app
reviews.text: I used to go to this Bible app very regularly, but there are now so many ads, I get very frustrated trying to accomplish anything on here. Are you aware that your app has pretty much turned into a Temu and game advertisement? I would rather pay a monthly fee and be ensured I could actually do what I want to do, than feel like a Temu hostage. I’ll be deleting this app and finding another.  Very sad about it.

reviews.title: For women only
reviews.text: I love this woman’s bible I may not read it daily like i should but i know I pray about it all the time🙏💕

reviews.title: Free version less than ideal
reviews.text:
I use the free version of the app. Two big things, I’m barely on Genesis 41 and in order to get to the Bible I have to open and close it multiple times to avoid the ads. Once I finish a chapter I then have to close out of the app and do it all over again because the ads won’t stop and the X never pops up to get rid of them. So not ideal that it takes double the time just to get through my daily reading. Also if you want to be lazy, want to hear how the names are said. Whatever reason and chose to listen to that chapter for the day, audio does not follow the version of scripture on the written page. Probably best to have the person reading use the same passage as in the app.
Other than that it’s about as good as any other Bible app.
